title: A lock traded for a dataclass
why: The class was rewritten as a dataclass and the lock went with the rewrite, while the lock is what made the counter safe for the threads the docstring still mentions. Nothing in the new lines is wrong on its own, so the defect is only visible against what the previous revision guaranteed. Two earlier versions of this case carried regressions the case did not intend: the total widened from an int to a float, then the generated `__eq__` made the object unhashable. All three models found the first, and Fable the second, so the type stays an int and `eq=False` keeps equality identity-based, leaving the lock as the only defect.

trusted.note: Both revisions read line by line. after/ keeps total an int and eq=False, so the only regression left is the dropped lock, and the docstring still advertises the thread safety it no longer has. The two earlier regressions are recorded in why; this note is what says they are gone, so a finding on the type or on hashability would be a false positive now.

planted.problem: The update no longer holds the lock, so two threads can read and write the total at once and one increment is lost
